prompt: Coreto's seat-hold code shows exactly how a hold works. By the lesson, what does an ADR add that the code lacks?

choices.text: A diagram of the module's classes and tables
choices.why: A diagram is another picture of what exists; the missing half is the reason it exists.

choices.text: Why it was chosen, and over what
choices.why: Right: the record keeps the reasons, in the terms of the moment the decision was taken.

choices.text: A step-by-step guide for changing the hold path safely
choices.why: That is a runbook. An ADR records a decision and its reasons, and gives no procedure.

choices.text: The list of engineers who approved the design
choices.why: Nygard's format has no approvers section; who signed matters less than why.

prompt: Match each ADR status to what it means.
hint: One status has a successor to point at; another has none.

pairs.right: The team is still arguing about it
The team committed, and the text is now fixed
A later record replaced it, and the two point at each other
It no longer applies, and nothing took its place

right_distractors: Rewritten to describe the current design

prompt: Coreto already writes an internal RFC before big changes. Why does the lesson say that is no substitute for an ADR?
hint: Before the decision, or after it?

choices.text: RFCs are too technical for product to read
choices.why: Audience is not the difference the lesson draws; an ADR is just as technical.

choices.text: An RFC lives in the wiki, and the wiki moves
choices.why: Location matters, but an RFC kept in the repository would still describe a proposal.

choices.text: It argues one option before the decision, and is rarely updated
choices.why: Right: a year on it shows what somebody wanted, and a reader cannot tell what was built.

choices.text: An RFC needs comments from the whole company, which slows every decision down
choices.why: Collecting objections is what an RFC is good at, by lesson 2 of the earlier course.

prompt: Which of these Coreto decisions pass the lesson's tests for earning a record? Choose all that apply.
hint: Expensive to reverse, or a "why" nobody could answer in a year.

choices.text: Buying a hosted search service instead of building one
choices.why: Yes: leaving a vendor is expensive, and the reasons depend on prices true this year.

choices.text: Upgrading a date-formatting library to its next minor version
choices.why: Cheap to reverse and nobody will ask why. A record here is noise in the log.

choices.text: Who decides how long a seat hold lasts
choices.why: Yes: a product decision in disguise, exactly the kind where somebody later asks who agreed.

choices.text: Holding seats with row locks in the database
choices.why: Yes: expensive to reverse, as two quarters of the Reservations team show.

choices.text: The Mobile team's choice of test runner for its own app
choices.why: One team's tooling preference is easy to change and touches no one else's code.

prompt: Coreto finally switches off its old reporting replica, and nothing replaces it. What happens to the ADR that chose the replica?
hint: Is there a successor record to point at?

choices.text: It is marked superseded
choices.why: Superseded needs a later record that replaced it, and here there is none to point at.

choices.text: It is deleted from the repository with the replica's code
choices.why: Deleting it removes the history of why the replica existed; the log keeps it.

choices.text: Its status changes to deprecated, and its text stays as written
choices.why: Right: the decision no longer applies and nothing took its place, which is what deprecated means.

choices.text: Its context is rewritten to explain the shutdown
choices.why: After acceptance the status line is the one part that moves; the shutdown is a new fact, not an edit.

prompt: Put the parts of a Nygard ADR in the order they appear in the file.
hint: The forces come before the choice they shape.
trap: Putting the decision before the context is how a context ends up arguing for a choice already made.

prompt: The Catalogue team drafts an ADR about search. Which title follows the lesson's advice?
hint: A title is the decision itself, not the area it concerns.

choices.text: Search
choices.why: A topic: a reader learns where to look and nothing about what was chosen.

choices.text: Review of the options for search relevance
choices.why: That names the discussion, not its outcome. The options belong in the context.

choices.text: Use a hosted search service
choices.why: Right: a short phrase that is the decision, readable at a glance in a long list.

choices.text: Search performance and relevance improvements for buyers
choices.why: A goal for the area; nothing in it says what the team will do.

prompt: What test does the lesson give for a well-written context?
hint: Think of the engineer who lost the argument.

choices.text: It makes the chosen option look clearly best
choices.why: That is the commonest fault: a context written after the decision, arguing for it.

choices.text: An engineer who preferred another option would call it fair
choices.why: Right: ADR-0006 gives the transaction fix its real advantage, the lowest cost, before rejecting it.

choices.text: It is shorter than the decision
choices.why: The lesson expects the context to take longer than the decision, since nobody can write it later.

choices.text: It cites the ticket numbers and names of the engineers involved
choices.why: Names and tickets belong to the plan, which changes weekly; the context holds the forces.

prompt: Nygard asks for the decision in full sentences and the active voice, so ADR-0006's decision opens with "We ___ record each hold as a row of its own".
hint: The future tense of a commitment.

prompt: ADR-0006's context says the strategy has put off microservices for a year. Why does the lesson want that sentence in the record?
hint: What happens when that fact stops being true?

choices.text: To record that the team judged microservices a mistake for Coreto
choices.why: The lesson says the opposite: without the sentence, the choice would look like that judgement.

choices.text: To link the ADR to the strategy document for audit
choices.why: Tracing is useful, but the point here is a reason that expires.

choices.text: So a later reader sees when a reason has gone and asks if the decision holds
choices.why: Right: facts of the moment go in the context, so their expiry is visible.

choices.text: To warn the Platform team off starting a migration
choices.why: An ADR is not a message to one team; the strategy already sets that order.

prompt: When ADR-0006 replaced ADR-0002, what changed in ADR-0002?

choices.text: Its context was updated to describe holds without locks
choices.why: That would erase the reasoning that was right at the time, which the log exists to keep.

choices.text: Its status line, which now names ADR-0006
choices.why: Right: the two records point at each other, and the old text stays as written.

choices.text: It was moved to an archive folder outside the repository
choices.why: Moving it breaks the trail; superseded records stay in place in the log.

choices.text: Its number was given to ADR-0006
choices.why: A number belongs to one record for good; reusing it would redirect every citation.

prompt: Why does the lesson say ADR-0002 should not be rewritten, even though its design is gone?
hint: A handful of venues, small on-sales.

choices.text: Rewriting it would break the links from pull requests that cite it
choices.why: The links follow the number, which would survive a rewrite; the loss is the reasoning.

choices.text: Locking rows was right for the Coreto of that time
choices.why: Right: without the old context, a future engineer sees only that somebody built something foolish.

choices.text: Accepted records are protected by a rule in the repository
choices.why: The lesson describes a discipline the team keeps, not a lock the tooling enforces.

choices.text: Nobody remembers the original reasons well enough
choices.why: ADR-0002 already holds a reconstructed context; the question is whether to keep it.

prompt: Coreto keeps its ADRs in docs/adr/ inside coreto-core. Which benefits does the lesson name for that placement? Choose all that apply.
hint: Review, search, and what happens when a module moves.

choices.text: A record is reviewed in the same pull request as the change
choices.why: Yes: an objection there costs a comment instead of a quarter.

choices.text: The CTO signs off each record before merge
choices.why: Nothing in the placement adds an approval step, and the lesson asks for none.

choices.text: An engineer finds it by searching the code they are reading
choices.why: Yes: no wiki login and no guessing which space it was filed in.

choices.text: Records move with the module when it leaves the monolith
choices.why: Yes: they travel in the same commit as the code they explain.

choices.text: Product managers read them in their weekly planning
choices.why: The lesson claims nothing about product reading the log; the benefits are for engineers at the code.

prompt: Why did ADR-0009 replace the deploy freeze in October rather than in March?
hint: What did ADR-0004 build, and what did it need before people trusted it?

choices.text: The on-sale season had ended by October, so the risk was lower
choices.why: The calendar is what the gate replaces; the lesson ties the timing to evidence.

choices.text: The load test had earned the team's trust
choices.why: Right: the freeze was right while nobody could measure a change, and ADR-0004 built the measurement.

choices.text: Helena asked the teams for fewer process rules this year
choices.why: No such request appears; the record cites the load test as its reason.

choices.text: ADR-0006 removed the locks, so deploys stopped being risky
choices.why: A deploy to the hold path still carries risk; the gate measures each change instead of banning dates.

prompt: A team inherits a ten-year-old system with no records at all. By the lesson, which old decisions are worth writing up late?
hint: A superseding record needs something to point at.

choices.text: Every decision still visible in the code, before new work starts
choices.why: Backfilling everything is a project nobody finishes; the lesson says it is not worth it.

choices.text: The ones the team is about to change
choices.why: Right: the honest old context is the best argument that the change is more than dislike of old code.

choices.text: The ones whose authors are still at the company
choices.why: Their authors help reconstruct a context, but that is how to write one, not which to write.

choices.text: The oldest ones, since they are the most at risk of being forgotten
choices.why: Age alone does not make a record useful; a decision nobody will touch can stay unwritten.

prompt: A company's ADR log reached 0012 last spring and has had no new record since, though the team kept making decisions. Which change does the lesson point to?
hint: How Coreto keeps the cost low.

choices.text: Require an architect's approval on each record
choices.why: An approval step raises the cost of writing a record, which is how logs die in the first place.

choices.text: A template in the folder and a checklist question in the pull request
choices.why: Right: the log stopped when the person who cared moved on, and these ask the question without them.

choices.text: Move the log to the wiki where more people will see it
choices.why: The wiki loses records the lesson's way: away from the code and the review.

choices.text: Expand the format so each record is a complete design document
choices.why: Records that grow into RFCs are one of the ways a log dies.

prompt: Once ADR-0009 took the place of the deploy freeze, the status line of ADR-0003 reads "___ by ADR-0009".
Payments and Checkout agree to retry failed card authorisations through a queue that both systems use. By Coreto's ADR-0001, where does the record go?
hint: One home, chosen once, by which system changes most.

choices.text: A copy in each of the two repositories
choices.why: Two copies drift apart, and then nobody knows which one is the decision.

choices.text: In a shared wiki page
choices.why: That takes the record away from the code and its review, the reasons the log lives in a repository.

choices.text: In the repository of the system the decision changes most
choices.why: Right: one home, by the rule ADR-0001 states; a platform-wide decision goes in coreto-core.

choices.text: Nowhere: a decision between two teams is an agreement, not architecture
choices.why: A retry path through a shared queue affects structure and dependencies, Nygard's test for significance.

prompt: Which line of ADR-0006 does the lesson call the most valuable?
hint: It hands a decision to somebody else.

choices.text: The rollback line: once the old path is deleted, going back takes a new record
choices.why: A useful line about reversibility, but it hands nothing to anybody outside the team.

choices.text: The hold length is a product decision, owned by Júlia's team
choices.why: Right: it hands product, in writing, a choice the technical change created.

choices.text: Buyers who lose a seat are told at once
choices.why: A real benefit, and the kind of line a list of only benefits would carry.

choices.text: The sweeper job needs an alert
choices.why: An honest cost, which helps the record be believed; the lesson ranks another line higher.
